v.why: With edge 3 absent, edge 5 is part of the only input-to-output path, so removing it disconnects the cell (-76/-62/-27 in experiment 45).
Filling a missing direct input-to-output edge with a conv adds a path and gains more than replacing an existing op (+78 in experiment 19, +19 on IN16 in experiment 84).
Removing a 3x3 conv loses real capacity and hurts on all three datasets (experiments 57, 62, 97), while removing other ops is roughly neutral.
Replacing a 3x3 conv with a skip connection loses accuracy on most datasets (experiments 2 and 68), unlike replacing 1x1 convs.
Upgrading a parameter-free skip on the final edge to a 3x3 conv gives consistent gains (experiments 65 and 95).
Deleting a 3x3 conv on the output edge is consistently harmful (experiments 1, 5, 45 and 70).
Parents with weak skip-heavy edges leave the most room, so a conv on the first edge gains much more (experiments 11 and 91).
Replacing a skip with a 3x3 conv on edge 4 gains consistently (experiments 14 and 89), more than adding it where the edge was none or already a conv.
Swapping a 1x1 conv for pooling on the direct edge helps on all three datasets (experiment 9) but is about neutral when replacing a 3x3 conv (experiment 3).
Replacing a skip with a 3x3 conv on the middle edge helps on all three datasets (experiments 58 and 63).
